endorsements.quote: To prioritize efforts, the problem to be solved should be well defined, and the overall value of each solution to the clinical practice should be assessed.

Iterative discovery and design processes, usability testing, and user feedback mechanisms are essential for identifying key user needs, workflow dimensions, and usability issues and refining AI interfaces to match clinicians’ mental models effectively.
This monitoring system should include user feedback, patient outcomes, and operational efficiency metrics to assess the AI solution’s real-world impact.
To ensure a deployed AI tool is useful to the practice, a rigorous postproduction monitoring system is necessary to track algorithm performance.
AI solutions should be directly integrated into clinicians’ daily workflows and seamlessly embedded into their everyday use patterns.
Thus, workflow validation is needed to assess the effective integration of the AI tool into the clinical workflow.
One important decision to be made when selecting a software solution is whether to purchase an existing product or to develop one using internal resources.
Selecting AI use cases based on institutional priorities helps align teams toward a common purpose.

unlisted_practices: Present AI outputs with relevant clinical context, such as EHR data, trends, and risk calculators, at the appropriate time in the workflow.
Allow clinicians to flag suspicious AI results and provide feedback to improve the algorithm and mitigate drift.
Internal development teams should develop software as a medical device products with the same care and rigor as external vendors.
Perform technical validation of AI algorithms for accuracy, reliability, fairness, and robustness across diverse datasets before clinical use.
Perform clinical validation of AI algorithms on independent datasets and in different settings, comparing with clinical outcomes.
Maintain human oversight or involvement in the clinical workflow to preserve accountability and safeguard against algorithm errors or bias.
Engage clinicians and other stakeholders for input and ongoing feedback throughout AI implementation, within the clinical workflow.
Institutional approval and prioritization should be required for cross-domain, multispecialty AI systems.
Weigh AI cost savings against the additional costs of support staff and infrastructure.

screen.reason: This is a framework/commentary paper providing strategic recommendations and institutional considerations for selecting and integrating AI solutions in healthcare.
